outputs.explanation: Panel A is a domain-map schematic plus representative western blot images, not a plot of averaged data.

The bar charts show densitometry quantification derived from the single representative blot shown in panel A for each antibody, not an average across multiple biological replicates. No replicate/error information is indicated, so there are no underlying individual data points to overlay.

Panel C is a heatmap of normalized abundances (averaged over 2 replicates per cell). Heatmaps display many protein x antibody values in a grid and are not a format where overlaying individual replicate points is standard or feasible; this check does not apply to this plot type.

The violin plots already depict the full distribution (shape/spread) of the underlying log2 enrichment ratios across the many co-isolated proteins, rather than collapsing the data to a single mean plus error bar, so overlaying individual points is not required. The orange HTT circle is a single highlighted bait value, not a summary statistic needing point-overlay.
Bars show mean ± SD (n = 4) for Htt, Hap40, and Synj1 abundances, and the individual replicate data points are overlaid as open circles on each bar.
Panel F is a sequence alignment and predicted crystal structure image, not a plot of averaged quantitative data.
Each point in the scatterplots is an individual co-isolated protein's enrichment ratio; the panel is not displaying an averaged summary statistic that would require underlying points.
The scatterplot explicitly plots log10 abundance values for HTT vs. HAP40 from each individual IP-MS experiment by tissue, so individual data points are already shown rather than an average.
This is a PCA scatterplot where each point represents an individual sample; it is not an averaged summary plot requiring point overlay.
Like panel I, these PCA scatterplots show individual samples as points stratified by antibody set and polyQ length/tissue; they are not averaged summary plots requiring additional point overlay.
